overview: One is the cell's total 'push' when no current is drawn; the other is what's actually measurable across any two points once current flows.
genZNote: EMF is the promise, potential difference is what actually shows up after the internal resistance takes its cut.

aspects.label: Definition
aspects.valueA: Energy supplied by the cell per unit charge, including work done against internal resistance.
aspects.valueB: Energy difference per unit charge between two points in a circuit (external, across a component).

aspects.label: When Equal to Terminal Voltage
aspects.valueA: Equals terminal voltage only when no current is drawn (open circuit).
aspects.valueB: Always less than EMF when current flows, due to voltage drop across internal resistance (V = ε − Ir).

aspects.label: Where It Applies
aspects.valueA: A property of the source (cell/battery) as a whole.
aspects.valueB: Can be measured between any two points in a circuit, not just across the source.

overlay.examHighYieldNote: V = ε − Ir is one of the most frequently tested current electricity relations.
overlay.commonMisconception: Treating EMF and terminal voltage as always equal — they match only at zero current.
